findings.title: Home profiles: the PDF page is not the sheet (contract: "MediaBox = A4 landscape, TrimBox = the spread centred in it")
findings.where: /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-layout/src/page.rs:96-101 (page_geometry: slug derived from min(mx,my)) and page.rs:160-163 (new_page)
findings.evidence: Failing tests in /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-layout/tests/spar_contract.rs: `home_a4_page_is_a4_landscape` -> "MediaBox must be A4 landscape (297 x 210 mm) around the centred spread, got Rect { x: -16.0, y: -16.0, w: 262.0, h: 210.0 }"; `home_media_box_is_the_sheet_for_every_preset_that_fits` -> "12 of 12 home pages are not the sheet" (poche on a4 262x210 vs 297x210; a6 on a4 282x210; poche on letter 267.9x215.9 vs 279.4x215.9; a6 on letter 279.4x207.4 vs 279.4x215.9; a5 on a3 393x297 vs 420x297; ...). No preset on any named sheet yields a page equal to the sheet. Consequence beyond the letter of the contract: front/back registration relies on the spread being centred on the physical sheet; with a non-standard page size that is left to how each PDF viewer/driver places a 262 mm page on A4 paper (centre vs top-left vs fit) instead of being fixed by the file. The implementer acknowledged this deviation; it is real and currently untested by their suite (their tests assert the 262x210 box).
findings.suggested_fix: Cannot be fixed inside ebc-layout alone: ebc_scene::Page has one scalar `slug`. Give Page a per-axis slug (slug_x/slug_y) or an explicit media rect and make ebc-pdf (writer.rs:199-216, content.rs:135) honour it; then new_page sets the media box from PageGeometry.sheet.sheet (already computed correctly) and mark_area can use the real printable rect. Until then the contract point is unmet and should be tracked as a cross-crate change.

findings.title: Fold marks are drawn exactly like crop marks on the press profile (and on home sheets with < 7 mm of margin)
findings.where: /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-layout/src/marks.rs:168-193 (fold_marks; solid ticks at line 177, dashed extension only for MarkStyle::Guide and only if >= 1 mm fits after tick + 1 mm gap)
findings.evidence: Failing tests in /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-layout/tests/spar_fold_marks.rs: `press_fold_marks_are_told_apart_from_crop_marks` -> "fold marks and crop marks are drawn identically on professional_eu; vertical ticks above the card as (x, from y, to y, solid): [(0.0, -3.0, -8.0, true), (110.0, -3.0, -8.0, true), (120.0, -3.0, -8.0, true), (230.0, -3.0, -8.0, true)]" (same stroke, colour, weight, offset, length: two mean cut, two mean crease). `home_fold_marks_stay_told_apart_on_a_tight_sheet` (110x186 mm cover on home A4) -> "with a 5 mm mark band the home fold marks are solid ticks identical to the cut marks (1 fold-mark item(s), none dashed)". Both research notes the crate cites say dashed: docs/research/notes/print-requirements.prepress.md line 42 ("fold marks for the two spine folds drawn the same way, dashed") and print-requirements.folding.md section 2 ("Dashed fold ticks vs solid crop marks is the DTP convention"). The caption the caption_areas docs suggest ("cut on the solid marks, fold on the dashed ones") would be wrong on such sheets.
findings.suggested_fix: Stroke the fold tick itself dashed (e.g. Stroke::dashed(color, weight, FOLD_GUIDE_DASH_MM)) for every MarkStyle, keeping the optional longer guide for home; update the `ticks solid, guide dashed` expectation in tests/invariants.rs check_fold_marks and the marks.rs unit test accordingly.

findings.title: target_px / min_px ask for one pixel too many on inch-based sizes, and an image at exactly the target (or minimum) resolution is judged Low (or TooLow)
findings.evidence: All 4 tests in /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-layout/tests/spar_resolution.rs fail. `target_px_of_a_6_by_9_inch_cover_is_1800_by_2700`: left (1801, 2700), right (1800, 2700) (152.4/25.4 = 6.000000000000001 in f64). `pixel_requirements_are_exact_on_inch_based_sizes`: 12 wrong, e.g. target_px(76.2 mm = 3 in at 300 ppi) = 901 expected 900; min_px(152.4 mm at 150 ppi) = 901 expected 900; target_px(177.8 mm) = 2101 expected 2100. `a_scan_at_exactly_300_ppi_is_good`: (1800, 2700) px on 152.4 x 228.6 mm -> effective_ppi 299.99999999999994 -> judge_ppi = Low, expected Good. `an_image_with_the_required_pixels_passes_the_verdict` (every size 50.00..300.00 mm step 0.01, both profiles, 50002 sizes): 13 sizes where exactly target_px pixels are judged Low (e.g. home: target_px(142.24) = 1120 px judged Low), 13 where exactly min_px pixels are judged TooLow ("a printer may reject it"), 139 where target_px is one pixel too high (checked with exact integer arithmetic). The implementer's own test hides this with a 1 ppi slack (tests/invariants.rs:907 `ppi >= profile.target_ppi - 1.0`).
findings.suggested_fix: In px_at snap before rounding up: `let v = mm * ppi / MM_PER_INCH; let r = v.round(); if (v - r).abs() <= 1e-9 * r.max(1.0) { r } else { v.ceil() }`. In judge_ppi compare with a relative tolerance (e.g. `ppi >= target * (1.0 - 1e-9)`), or compute effective_ppi as `px * MM_PER_INCH / mm` and still compare with tolerance. Then tighten invariants.rs:907 to `>= target_ppi`.

findings.title: The documented full-bleed cover recipe places every cover bleed/2 off-centre (1.5 mm pro, 1 mm home): the fold hides ~0.4 mm, the fore-edge trim removes ~3.4 mm
findings.where: /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-layout/src/lib.rs:33-36 (doc example), src/image.rs:25-26 (place_image doc: "pass the panel with its bleed"), src/format.rs:68-87 (Panels::with_bleed grows outer edges only, so its centre is not the panel's centre)
findings.evidence: Failing tests in /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-layout/tests/spar_cover_placement.rs. `the_documented_recipe_centres_the_cover_on_its_panel`: for all 4 presets x 2 profiles x front/back, e.g. "poche front (professional_eu): hides 0.35 mm on the left and 3.35 mm on the right; the cover is +1.50 mm off the panel's centre", "poche back: hides 3.35 mm on the left and 0.35 mm on the right; -1.50 mm". `a_framed_cover_keeps_equal_margins_on_the_finished_poche_card`: a cover scan with a frame 6 mm inside its edges ends up "5.85 mm from the fold but 2.85 mm from the fore-edge after trimming" (expected equal; bordered covers come out visibly lopsided, centred titles sit 1.5 mm off the panel centre). place_image itself does what it says (centres in the target); the defect is the recipe the crate documents, which ebc-card (not yet written) will follow.
findings.suggested_fix: Provide and document a helper for covers, e.g. `cover_image_rect(panel, bleed, image_px, fit)` that places against `panel.inflate(bleed)` (symmetric about the panel) and returns the with_bleed rect as the clip; or change the docs/doctest to `place_image(px, panel.inflate(bleed), Fit::Cover)` clipped to `with_bleed(..)`. Alternatively expose alignment so the spine-side overhang equals the bleed.

findings.title: Landscape-first orientation leaves tall cards without any cut or fold guides although the same sheet in portrait has centimetres of room
findings.where: /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-layout/src/page.rs:88-94 (page_geometry: landscape whenever it fits, portrait only as fallback)
findings.evidence: Failing tests in /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-layout/tests/spar_home_sheet.rs. `a_tall_card_on_a4_gets_its_cut_and_fold_guides` (50x195 mm cover, 10 mm spine, home A4): "no cut or fold guides at all: the sheet is used in landscape with a 0.5 mm mark band, although A4 portrait leaves 50 mm around this 110 x 195 mm spread" - marks() returns an empty layer, new_page returns Ok, nothing signals it. `the_orientation_with_room_for_marks_is_chosen_when_there_is_one`: 10 of 1238 grid cases where both orientations fit lose all marks (e.g. 50..90 x 195 mm on A4: band 0.5 mm vs 43/33/23/13/3 mm the other way; 50..90 x 200 mm on Letter: 0.95 mm vs 32.7..6 mm). Only custom formats whose spread is taller than wide are affected; presets are not.
findings.suggested_fix: When both orientations fit, choose the one with the larger tighter margin min(mx, my) (ties -> landscape); the existing invariant `landscape is preferred whenever it works` in tests/invariants.rs then needs relaxing to that rule.

overall:
ebc-layout is robust where the implementer concentrated: I could not make it panic, emit non-finite geometry, draw a mark into the bleed, outside the mark area/printable area, or onto another mark. The problems I could demonstrate are one unmet contract point and four correctness/design defects at the edges, each with a failing test.

Demonstrated (12 failing tests in 5 files under /home/user/ebook-cadeau/crates/ebc-layout/tests/):
1. Major: home pages are never the sheet (0 of 12 preset/sheet combinations). The implementer disclosed this; it needs a change in ebc-scene::Page and ebc-pdf, so a fixer limited to ebc-layout cannot turn spar_contract.rs green alone.
2. Minor: fold marks are indistinguishable from crop marks on the press profile, and on home sheets with under 7 mm of margin; the project's own research notes call for dashed fold marks.
3. Minor: target_px/min_px return one pixel too many on inch-based sizes (6 in at 300 ppi -> 1801), and an image at exactly the target or minimum ppi is judged Low or TooLow. The existing invariants test masks this with a 1 ppi slack.
4. Minor: the cover-placement recipe in the crate docs shifts every cover by bleed/2 towards the fore-edge (1.5 mm on the professional profile); a framed cover ends up 5.85 mm from the fold and 2.85 mm from the fore-edge.
5. Minor: landscape-first orientation gives tall custom cards an empty marks layer with no signal, although portrait has room.

Tried without breaking anything (kept as 8 passing regression tests):
- 40,000 random and 300 directed format/profile combinations at the validation limits (100 mm bleed/slug/offset/unprintable margin, 2 pt strokes, 3 mm spines on 50 mm covers, sheets from exact fit to 5080 mm, both mark styles), with an independent ink-rectangle model: no ink in the bleed box, none outside mark area/media/printable area, no collisions between mark kinds, caption areas free, refusals always justified.
- 60,000 inputs with arbitrary f64 bit patterns in every field at once (NaN payloads, subnormals, signed zeros, infinities): no panic, invalid input always gives empty layers, anything that validates is a finite, nested page.
- place_image over extreme pixel sizes on sane targets: finite, covers/contains.
- info_entries for 20,000 formats read back with the same parsing and 0.1 mm rules as ebc-preflight's check_ebc_geometry: consistent.
- by_name lookups, error ordering and the contract's names/struct fields: fine.

Not counted as findings:
- docs/research/03-print-requirements.md still does not exist. The raw notes' proposed house spec (print-requirements.prepress.md section 8) says 5 mm safety margin and a 6 mm spine text band; professional_eu uses 4 mm and 7 mm. Reconcile when the consolidated document lands.
- A home page that fits with under 1 mm of mark band (e.g. spread height 194-196 mm on A4) returns Ok with an empty marks layer; callers must check page_geometry().mark_band_mm() themselves.
- Marks gains two fields beyond the contract (style, scale_ruler), so a struct literal written from the contract text will not compile; allowed by "add what the implementation needs".
